title: French high school protests: 'Young people are not fooled by the discrimination and contempt that society directs at them'
subhead: Sociologist and child psychiatrist Laelia Benoit analyzes the discourse surrounding high school student protests through the lens of 'childism,' a term that refers to the set of prejudices against minors based on their age, which she introduced to France.

Canadian writer Anne Carson awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in literature
subhead: The Canadian writer received the Swedish Academy's highest honor on Thursday, October 8. A master of textual deviation, Carson, who began as a classical philologist, blends poetry and popular culture, prose and verse, with both humor and erudition.

title: 'Russian journalist Anna Politkovskaya believed that a society that accepts lies ends up accepting violence as well'
subhead: Twenty years ago, the journalist was murdered at the instigation of Russian security services. Documentary filmmaker Eric Bergkraut, who knew her well, recalls her fight for truth and against Kremlin propaganda – a struggle that is more necessary than ever as Vladimir Putin continues to kill.

title: 'The Social Reckoning': Aaron Sorkin dives into toxic effects of Facebook and Instagram
subhead: The film, billed as a sequel to David Fincher's excellent 'The Social Network' about the creation of Facebook, fails to convince, either in its performances or its screenplay.

title: In Los Angeles, Nithya Raman wants to bring the new left to city hall
subhead: The 45-year-old Harvard graduate, who was born in India, will face off against LA Mayor Karen Bass on November 3. The Democratic showdown highlights the rise of the socialist movement, championed by New York's Zohran Mamdani and Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed.

subhead: The French health authorities reported that 8,124 deaths were related to the extreme heatwaves between late May and late August in France. Le Monde spoke to the friends and families of 11 of the victims to find out about the lives behind those numbers.

title: 'The French government's condescension toward high school students shows a refusal to take them seriously as citizens'
subhead: Before attempting to open dialogue, the French government handled the current high school student protests as if they were urban riots, sociologist Vincent Tiberj observes in an interview.

title: CEO of finance giant Pimco: 'Markets are sending France a serious signal. The situation is grave'
subhead: In an interview with Le Monde, the chief executive of one of the world's largest asset managers warns of France's worsening budget deficit and political instability. He clarifies that while he is 'not withdrawing' his investments in French debt, he is 'not increasing' them either.
